name: Python Foundations
description: Your first step into writing code. Starts from absolute zero with no prior programming experience assumed, and finishes with you building small working scripts on your own.

name: Full-Stack Web Development
description: Build and ship complete web applications end to end, covering both the browser side and the server side, with a deployed portfolio project by the final week.

name: Data Analysis with Pandas
description: Turn messy spreadsheets into clear answers. Focuses on cleaning real-world datasets, spotting trends, and producing charts that non-technical colleagues can actually read.

name: Machine Learning Essentials
description: How predictive models actually work and when to trust them. Covers the core algorithms, how to evaluate a model honestly, and the traps that make results look better than they are.

name: Deep Learning for Language
description: Work with transformers and large language models hands-on. Assumes you are already comfortable with machine learning fundamentals and want to build systems that understand text.

name: UX Design Fundamentals
description: Learn why people get confused by interfaces and how to fix it. Research, wireframing, and usability testing taught through redesigning products that frustrate their users.

name: Brand and Visual Identity
description: Craft a coherent visual identity from scratch, covering typography, colour systems, and logo work, ending with a full brand guideline document for a real client brief.

name: Cloud Architecture on AWS
description: Design infrastructure that stays up under load and does not bankrupt you. Covers scaling, redundancy, and cost control, and prepares you for the associate architect certification.

name: DevOps and CI/CD Pipelines
description: Automate the path from commit to production. Containers, pipelines, and monitoring, aimed at teams tired of manual deployments breaking on Friday afternoons.

name: Cybersecurity Essentials
description: Understand how systems get broken into and how to defend them. Covers common attack patterns, safe password and network practice, and a practical incident response walkthrough.

name: Penetration Testing in Practice
description: Authorised offensive security testing in a controlled lab. You attack deliberately vulnerable systems to learn how defenders should think, with a written engagement report at the end.

name: Digital Marketing Strategy
description: Get found online and turn attention into customers. Search visibility, paid campaigns, and email, with a focus on measuring whether any of it is actually working.

name: Product Management Foundations
description: Decide what to build and defend that decision. Roadmapping, prioritisation, and stakeholder conversations, for engineers and designers moving into a product role.

name: Confident Public Speaking
description: For people who dread presenting. Practical work on nerves, structure, and delivery, built around weekly recorded practice with feedback rather than theory.

name: Financial Modelling for Startups
description: Build the spreadsheet that convinces investors. Forecasting, unit economics, and valuation, taught by constructing a complete model for a fictional early-stage company.
